### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ActionParamSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ActionParamSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd586522046f69f9dfa3840c87b6a76e747fd7a9` — the merge of head `c89eef4e3be9f3f2e58d52a286513a56b1aec0f1` into base `8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd586522046f69f9dfa3840c87b6a76e747fd7a9 && git checkout dd586522046f69f9dfa3840c87b6a76e747fd7a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759 c89eef4e3be9f3f2e58d52a286513a56b1aec0f1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759 && git merge --no-ff c89eef4e3be9f3f2e58d52a286513a56b1aec0f1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8133cc78052c95b6efd59487b64fe78f69860759` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c89eef4e3be9f3f2e58d52a286513a56b1aec0f1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts + objectui packages/fields/src/resolveActionParams.ts at the console pin f8267df93aba8fb09cc1cc0692eadc0c8c5a5e56 (lines 235-269, 485-517, 563-591 and 649-651, the lines the new docblock cites and the inline branch it sits beside); read as well for sections ② and ③: packages/spec/src/ui/action.test.ts (the hunk at 1755-1759), .changeset/24047-action-param-options-comments.md, packages/spec/package.json (the files array) and packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md at 40254 and 73939. ### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #24047 (body and all four comments, the dev report 6226612936 included), PR #24072 (body, three-file list, net diff against main at the head), the 41 check-runs on the head, the two spec files and the changeset at the head, and the objectui file at the pin.

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The spec diff is 34 changed lines (action.zod.ts 17+/12-, action.test.ts 3+/2-) and every one of them is a `*` or `//` comment line; no Zod expression, no alias row, no `guidance` string (lines 120-126, 143-147 and 322-325 are untouched), no export and no message text moves. The schema face is hit by path alone. The check-runs agree: `TypeScript Type Check` (which carries check:api-surface, check:docs, check:authorable-surface and the rest of check:generated) and `Spec property liveness` both conclude success on the head.
- **Public surface: the docblock IS published, so its sentences are the surface under review.** `@objectstack/spec`'s `files` array ships `src/**/*.zod.ts`, so the rewritten TSDoc in action.zod.ts 268-279 goes into the tarball verbatim. Each factual sentence it makes about objectui, judged at the cited lines of the pin:
  1. "At the console pin (`.objectui-sha` f8267df93aba)" — `.objectui-sha` at the head reads f8267df93aba8fb09cc1cc0692eadc0c8c5a5e56. True.
  2. "`packages/fields/src/resolveActionParams.ts` resolves it as `authoredOptions ?? normaliseOptions(field.options, …)` (`:650`–`:651`)" — pin lines 650-651 are `const resolvedOptions = authoredOptions` / `?? normaliseOptions(field.options, ownerName, param.field, ctx.fieldOptionLabel);`, inside the field-backed branch (the inline branch returns at 568-591, the unresolved-field branch at 597-647). True.
  3. "`normaliseOptions` returns `{ ...raw, label, value: raw.value }` per entry (`:515`)" — pin line 515 is exactly that statement, the return of the `options.map` at 510-516 of the function declared at 503. True.
  4. "so every key of an inherited entry survives the resolver" — `raw` is the entry itself for an object entry (511, a bare string becomes `{ label, value }`), spread first, then `label` (translated through `fieldOptionLabel` when one is supplied, 512-514) and `value` reassigned. No key is dropped. One qualifier the docblock does not need: an absent, non-array or empty `field.options` resolves to `undefined` (509), which is not a key drop. True.
  5. "An authored `options` array still wins over the inherited one" — `authoredOptions = resolveOptionLabels(param.options, ctx.locale)` (565) is `undefined` only when `param.options` is `undefined` (250), so the `??` at 650 reaches the inherited list only then. True.
  6. "no reader of `color` / `icon` / `disabled` on an inherited option is measured from this repo" — a claim about this repo. action.test.ts at the head pins no inherited-path reader (its only inheritance tests, at 47-105, are about widget config and lookup omission), and a tree-wide grep at the head finds no liveness row, skill or doc page measuring one. True as written, and it is the exact wording the card's rule 2 asked for: the keys survive, the readers are unmeasured, so the `guidance` strings keep refusing the field-backed prescription.
- **The comment above the `guidance` table (310-317)** restates 3-4 and defers to the docblock for the pin and line, which the docblock carries. Consistent and true.
- **The card's "Done when" holds.** A grep of packages/spec/src at the head for the old sentence ("rebuilds each/every inherited entry") returns nothing; the three places now say the keys are kept by spread; the citations are the pin's own lines (`:515`, `:650`-`:651`, pin sha), not the card's `:503` at objectui main 94b2489f, as the card required.
- **Wrong: nothing.** No derived judgment in the diff is false.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/24047-action-param-options-comments.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` with `Clause-②: no` in its body; the PR body's second line is `Clause-②: no`. The two agree and both are right: the diff adds, removes or renames no key, accepted value, export or message text, so `no` with no arm is the declaration, and `skip-changeset` ("publishes nothing from any released package") would be false because the rewritten TSDoc ships in the tarball (`files` includes `src/**/*.zod.ts`). `patch` is the lowest level that is not a lie. Precedent at the head: `.changeset/23012-lookup-snake-tolerance-text.md`, the same class (docblock-only patch on spec, `Clause-②: no`).
- The card allowed "no changeset, or a prose-only patch changeset if a gate requires one"; `Check Changeset` requires a changeset or the `skip-changeset` label, the dispatch gave the dev no label write, and the label would have been false anyway. The route taken is the accurate one.
- Gates: `Check Changeset` success; check-changeset-no-major (no `major`; the level axis asks nothing of a `Clause-②: no` PR) and check-adr-0087-registration (no breaking declaration, no marker owed) ride in `Lint & Repo Gates`, success. `Clause-②:` line: `no`, matching the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report (6226612936) declares `open_questions: []`, two `out_of_scope_findings`, two deviations and one housekeeping note. Each:

- **Flag: the `visibleWhen` bullet (action.zod.ts 249-259) still quotes the inline branch as `options: param.options`.** Verified at the pin: 565 `const authoredOptions = resolveOptionLabels(param.options, ctx.locale)`, 574 `options: authoredOptions`; `resolveOptionLabels` (246-269) returns the same array object when every label is already a string (257) and otherwise rebuilds by spread with each label resolved (258-268). So the bullet's point (the inline list is lowered verbatim, keys intact) holds for a string-labelled list and the quoted expression is stale; for an inline per-locale label the list is rebuilt by spread, so "verbatim" is loose there too. Pre-existing, outside the card's "Done when" (that bullet never claimed a `{ label, value }` rebuild) and outside the claim's file surface, so the dev was right not to widen. Answered: not a defect of this diff. Escalated to the adopting seat: it is the same class as this card (a published docblock sentence about objectui that drifted), so a sibling comment card is the better carrier than an acceptance note alone.
- **Flag: packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md 40254 (under 17.0.0) and 73939 (under 17.0.0-rc.6) describe the drop.** Read at the head: both are the same paragraph, headed "本次**没有**修的一件事(objectui 侧,已另行记录)", written in that release's own tense — a record of what objectui did when that release shipped, not a claim about today's pin. Release-owned (Documentation Guardrails): a factual error in a released entry goes in a dedicated docs-only PR, never a rider. No factual error is established (objectui's fbc23e094 is cited by the pin's own docblock as the later change), so nothing is owed by this PR. Answered: acceptance note is the right carrier.
- **Deviation: no labels written.** The gates are green without one; nothing owed.
- **Deviation: `main` merged once before the PR opened.** The head is that merge commit, GitHub reports it mergeable and clean, the dev re-verified spec build, tests, typecheck and check:generated on it, and all 41 check-runs are on this head. Nothing owed.
- **Housekeeping: a temp file written into the PM's scratch directory and deleted.** Not in the diff (three files); nothing owed.
- **Readers measurement (the card's rule 2: "if you measure the readers, put it in the PR body").** The PR body carries a static source read at the pin and the comments say "not measured from this repo" rather than "no reader". Spot-checked at the pin: ActionParamDialog.tsx 536 re-spreads each option with a localised label; paramToField.ts 102 passes `options: param.options` through; SelectField.tsx 227-230 renders `option.value` and `optionDisplayLabel(option)`, which reads `label` and `value` only (optionRules.ts 173-176); every `disabled` in the four widgets is `props.disabled` (SelectField 213, MultiSelectField 201, RadioField 129, CheckboxesField 163); no `.color` or `.icon` read in the four files. The reading supports leaving the `guidance` strings alone, and the PR proposes no `guidance` change, as the card required.
- **Check-runs on the head: 41, none failed.** All five required contexts conclude success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (6/6 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, the three claim guards and `Flag docs affected by code changes` are success. The seven skipped runs are path-filtered or opt-in (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the two Dogfood jobs, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance) and none is a required context. The dev left test:repo to CI; Test Core answers it.
- **Governance.** No governed-surface path in the file list; head repo equals base repo (not a fork); size/s, 48 changed lines; draft; the PR's assignee (huangyiirene) matches the card's after the takeover, and the newest `Claim:` (6228783833) names this branch.
